sourceLocation.atomicFragment: Manifest completeness is established under the same omission-challenge discipline this specification imposes on project content.

requirements.controllingText: Manifest completeness is established under the same omission-challenge discipline this specification imposes on project content. One extractor drafts the manifest from the controlling text; an independent reviewer that did not receive the draft performs its own extraction or section-by-section coverage pass; a distinct reconciliation resolves every difference; and every specification section is either covered by entries or explicitly recorded as nonnormative with a reason. CI records the challenge and reconciliation evidence with the manifest digest. An unreconciled material disagreement, an uncovered section, or a missing challenge record blocks acceptance.

sourceLocation.atomicFragment: File-inspection status is the closed set INCLUDED_IN_HANDOFF, which the application establishes; EXTERNAL_INSPECTION_CLAIMED, which is agent-asserted; INSPECTION_SUPPORTED, which is the claim plus complete consistent per-unit dispositions and source locations; and INSPECTION_ESTABLISHED_TO_REQUIRED_BASIS, which is the minimum basis the file's contract requires.

requirements.controllingText: File-inspection status is the closed set INCLUDED_IN_HANDOFF, which the application establishes; EXTERNAL_INSPECTION_CLAIMED, which is agent-asserted; INSPECTION_SUPPORTED, which is the claim plus complete consistent per-unit dispositions and source locations; and INSPECTION_ESTABLISHED_TO_REQUIRED_BASIS, which is the minimum basis the file's contract requires. Stage 01 completion requires INCLUDED_IN_HANDOFF as an application fact and at least INSPECTION_SUPPORTED for every required file; the word inspected always means at the recorded basis and is never represented as an application-proven semantic fact. A required artifact whose semantic content is INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED and not proven immaterial leaves Stage 01 BLOCKED unless human authority removes it from project scope through a new input version.

sourceLocation.atomicFragment: The unitization contract explicitly defines treatment of comments

requirements.controllingText: The unitization contract explicitly defines treatment of comments, annotations, tracked changes, metadata, embedded objects, inaccessible content, and unsupported formats. A supported subdivision cannot be replaced by one whole-file unit merely to make coverage vacuous. SEMANTIC_CHALLENGE_LIMITS/1 triggers a challenge when any one of these thresholds is exceeded: 1,048,576 stored bytes in one text or document artifact; 100 mechanically countable pages; 20 supplied files or archive members; 500 raw units; or 5,242,880 aggregate supplied bytes. A material uncovered unit, broad exclusion, INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED material, material uncertainty, contradiction, or operator request triggers regardless of size. These limits are centralized, versioned, and acceptance-tested and may be lowered but not raised without a new contract-profile identity.

requirements.controllingText: The versioned source-class checklist derives from the closed generic class set — governing law and regulation; standards and specifications; controlling contracts and prior agreements; authoritative technical documentation; official registries and databases; scholarly and measurement literature; and project-supplied references — filtered by the Stage 01 objective and declared jurisdiction or system scope. The contract also declares explicit stopping criteria: every registered location searched; query saturation, meaning no new candidate source in the final registered query round; authority-chain closure, meaning every authority cited by an accepted controlling source received a disposition; the declared date or version cutoff; a disposition for every inaccessible location; and the residual-risk statement. Search completion without every declared criterion is invalid.

sourceLocation.atomicFragment: When staging or raw capture fails, canonical state does not change.

requirements.controllingText: When staging or raw capture fails, canonical state does not change. The application preserves the staged bytes and slot identities when technically possible, identifies exactly what was and was not recorded, and permits retry without opening or pasting the file. When the browser requires reselection, the UI identifies the exact prior filename, size, and digest and classifies reselection as an unavoidable file action rather than repeated semantic resupply. The application never claims an uncaptured response was recorded.

sourceLocation.atomicFragment: When clarification occurs outside the application, the final response may report the answer but cannot write a HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION field.

requirements.controllingText: When clarification occurs outside the application, the final response may report the answer but cannot write a HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION field. An external agent may return the answer only as a proposed extracted human-origin value in humanAuthorityCandidates; the application MUST NOT classify that agent-reported value as HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION until the operator confirms or corrects it in the application. The application compares the reported answer with existing human records. A new human-origin value is presented for confirm or correct and recorded through a dedicated human command. Confirmation MUST be one-tap or direct edit of the proposed value; no retyping is required. Exact confirmation may use atomic co-acceptance under Section 14.10; a correction or inconsistency creates a new input version and replacement prompt. Confirmation does not apply to information already supplied.

sourceLocation.atomicFragment: Every artifact preserves rawFilename and has a safe displayFilename and canonicalPath under closed-loop-filename/1.

requirements.controllingText: Every artifact preserves rawFilename and has a safe displayFilename and canonicalPath under closed-loop-filename/1. Canonical comparison uses Unicode 15.1.0 NFC, case-sensitive identity, and separately checked Unicode 15.1.0 default-case-fold and registered platform-risk collision keys. Absolute paths, drive prefixes, NUL, control characters, empty segments, `.` and `..`, duplicate canonical paths, case-fold collisions, extraction-target collisions, and supported confusable collisions are rejected. An unauthorized rename never matches solely because bytes are equal.

requirements.controllingText: When author and reviewer disagree materially, neither output is promoted. A human may decide only an actual human authority, policy, scope, risk, disclosure, or tradeoff question. Every unresolved disagreement remains UNKNOWN or BLOCKED and is never automatically promoted.

requirements.controllingText: NFC normalization and default case folding use Unicode 15.1.0 data. Confusable detection uses the Unicode Technical Standard #39 confusables data published for Unicode 15.1.0. These exact data identities and table digests are recorded in the runtime registry and deployment manifest. A host Unicode implementation may be used only when startup and CI conformance fixtures establish the pinned results for every supported code-point class; otherwise the application uses bundled pinned tables. An unknown host/table mismatch blocks canonical filename normalization and package activation. Runtime upgrades do not silently change canonical identities; runtime or browser Unicode behavior may not silently redefine canonical identity. Every set-valued array has one named versioned normalizer. Every contentSha256, recordSha256, project hash, package hash, proof hash, scope hash, and terminal hash has a closed JSON-pointer inclusion and omission set registered in workflow-schema.js. No implementation selects preimage fields implicitly.

requirements.controllingText: For every registered hash kind, the preimage inclusion set is exactly the canonical fields of the subject record or manifest, excluding only the digest field itself and every field whose value depends on that digest, fields declared audit-only or derived-summary, and fields the owning schema explicitly excludes with a registered reason. The scope-hash preimage is exactly the Section 14.7 dimensions of the operation, and the terminal-hash preimage is exactly the records enumerated in Section 36.9. An unregistered hash kind or pointer set is UNDEFINED_HASH_PREIMAGE and blocks the computation and every dependent gate. Default array semantics are ordered and order-significant; an array is set-valued only when its JSON pointer is explicitly registered with an element-identity key, a duplicate rule that rejects duplicates, and a sort rule of canonical byte order over the element identity. An unregistered pointer treated as a set is UNDEFINED_SET_SEMANTICS and blocks.

requirements.controllingText: Reservation states are RESERVED, EXPORTED, ORPHANED, RESUMED, RESPONSE_STAGED, ACCEPTED, REJECTED, CANCELLED, SUPERSEDED, or EXPIRED_BY_SCOPE. Only RESERVED, EXPORTED, ORPHANED, RESUMED, and RESPONSE_STAGED can preserve package validity, and only when revision, scope, prompt, package, nonce, and target slot remain unchanged. EXPORTED, ORPHANED, RESUMED, RESPONSE_STAGED, REJECTED, and CANCELLED are recorded as metadata-store operational events and do not increment canonical projectRevision. ACCEPTED commits the canonical project once. A later canonical scope change marks the reservation SUPERSEDED or EXPIRED_BY_SCOPE. No operational status event invalidates its own package.

sourceLocation.atomicFragment: closed-loop-encrypted-export/1 uses AES-256-GCM with a fresh 96-bit cryptographically random IV per encrypted payload

requirements.controllingText: closed-loop-encrypted-export/1 uses AES-256-GCM with a fresh 96-bit cryptographically random IV per encrypted payload, a fresh 128-bit random salt, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 with 600,000 iterations to derive the 256-bit key from the operator passphrase, and the canonical unencrypted package manifest digest as authenticated additional data. The container records algorithm, KDF, iterations, salt, IV, ciphertext length, and authentication tag. The passphrase and derived key are never persisted. IV reuse under one key is prohibited. Authentication failure rejects the export or restore without partial activation. CREDENTIAL_SECRET backup material requires this encrypted profile and cannot use an acknowledgment-only unencrypted export.

requirements.controllingText: A BLOCKED delivery record is a terminal determination record, not an authorization. The command's own committed revision is part of the record and does not invalidate it. Only a later revision that changes a dependency in the recorded terminal dependency closure can supersede, block, or withdraw it. Registry incompleteness blocks Stage 30; it does not mutate Stage 27 into a dependency cycle. A registry finding that objectively refutes an earlier premise invalidates that premise through the responsible-stage map and requires recalculation in order.

sourceLocation.atomicFragment: The application records a DELIVERY_ATTEMPT receipt containing the delivery ID

requirements.controllingText: The application records a DELIVERY_ATTEMPT receipt containing the delivery ID, attempt ID, exact artifacts, byte hashes, operator action, intended recipient/destination/channel, device-reported time, result, and available external receipt. When the requested outcome includes delivery to the operator or another destination, Stage 30 workflow completion requires at least one successful authorized export or share attempt within the delivery record's scope. DELIVERY_STATE = AUTHORIZED permits the UI to say "Delivery authorized." It may say "Delivery attempted" only after the action receipt exists. It may say "Delivered" only when current evidence attributable to the recipient, destination, channel, or external system establishes transfer at its actual epistemic basis. The application cannot prevent or count transfers performed outside its controlled action path and must display that limitation. It does not claim it can undo a completed external transfer.

requirements.controllingText: The application records a DELIVERY_ATTEMPT receipt containing the delivery ID, attempt ID, exact artifacts, byte hashes, operator action, intended recipient/destination/channel, device-reported time, result, and available external receipt. When the requested outcome includes delivery to the operator or another destination, Stage 30 workflow completion requires at least one successful authorized export or share attempt within the delivery record's scope. DELIVERY_STATE = AUTHORIZED permits the UI to say "Delivery authorized." It may say "Delivery attempted" only after the action receipt exists. It may say "Delivered" only when current evidence attributable to the recipient, destination, channel, or external system establishes transfer at its actual epistemic basis. The application cannot prevent or count transfers performed outside its controlled action path and must display that limitation. It does not claim it can undo a completed external transfer.

requirements.controllingText: Completion: Defect and regression histories are append-only; corrections are new records; every confirmed defect has a permanent regression; every due applicable regression execution is current; the pre-delivery checkpoint exists; CALCULATE_TERMINAL atomically creates one AUTHORIZED or BLOCKED delivery determination under Section 36.9. Export or share and any delivery completion are separately receipted and never inferred from authorization. Stage 30 closes through the one atomic CALCULATE_TERMINAL command, which reads the precondition revision, validates registry integrity and all terminal prerequisites, creates exactly one current terminal determination, sets DELIVERY_STATE = AUTHORIZED only when every prerequisite is true and otherwise BLOCKED, increments revision once, and commits once. The command's own committed revision does not invalidate its result; only a later revision affecting its dependency closure may supersede or withdraw it. Registry incompleteness blocks Stage 30 unless it proves an earlier premise false; it does not create a Stage 27↔Stage 30 cycle.

sourceLocation.atomicFragment: Because the canonical handoff container is logical under Section 19.7, per-member sequential export or share on the pinned device satisfies package export whenever a combined multi-file share is unavailable; the optional archive representation is never required.

requirements.controllingText: Because the canonical handoff container is logical under Section 19.7, per-member sequential export or share on the pinned device satisfies package export whenever a combined multi-file share is unavailable; the optional archive representation is never required. Before the acceptance run, the acceptance procedure executes a recorded MOBILE_CAPABILITY_PROBE on the pinned target covering file export or share, response-file selection, returned-file slot selection, persistent-storage request, logical package export, and backup export and restore. A required capability the pinned target cannot perform yields BLOCKED with the exact missing capability recorded. The only permitted continuations are a new pinned target record on an iOS or Safari version that supports the capability, or a governance change to the controlling specification. No silent degradation path exists.

requirements.controllingText: Before deployment, CI creates closed-loop-deployment-manifest/1 from the audited source commit. It lists canonical origin/base path, source commit, workflow run, build identity, canonicalization and registry identities, build command/environment, workflow-file digest, dependency/lockfile identities, CSP value, and every runtime HTML, JavaScript, CSS, worker, icon, manifest, schema, and asset path with media type, byte length, hash algorithm, and digest. The deployment manifest carries one overall manifest digest computed under closed-loop-canonical-json/1 with the digest field itself omitted; no manifest digest includes itself. Unmanifested runtime resources are prohibited.

sourceLocation.atomicFragment: The application has no controlling service worker unless it is explicitly required

requirements.controllingText: The application has no controlling service worker unless it is explicitly required, manifested, versioned, security-reviewed, and tested. Clean-profile and previously cached-profile acceptance must load one unmixed build identity or visibly block as stale. The running page, every script and style, and test-worker.js report or are bound to the expected build. Post-deployment verification retrieves every manifest path with cache bypass where supported and rejects missing, extra, redirected-to-different-content, cross-origin, stale, or modified resources. Browser acceptance proves the executed HTML, JavaScript, CSS, and worker resource graph matches the same manifest and build identity; mixed or stale cached builds fail.

sourceLocation.atomicFragment: An AUTHORIZED terminal determination proves authorization, not physical transfer.

requirements.controllingText: An AUTHORIZED terminal determination proves authorization, not physical transfer. Stage 30 therefore exposes the non-stage-increasing terminal action EXPORT_OR_SHARE_AUTHORIZED_ARTIFACTS. Immediately before export or share, the application reverifies the exact authorized bytes and current terminal dependency closure, performs the browser-supported export or share action, and records a DELIVERY_ATTEMPT receipt in the deliveryAttempts family with its actual evidence basis.
